note: SBLGNT (with the earliest manuscripts) reads Asaph, probably Matthew's own spelling or a play on the psalmist; TR "asa" corrects it to the king's name (also 1:8).
Earliest manuscripts read Amos (possibly echoing the prophet); TR "amon" harmonises with 2 Kings 21.

kjv: till she (Mary) had brought forth her firstborn son
mine: until she (Mary) had given birth to a son
note: TR adds "ton prototokon" ("her firstborn") from Luke 2:7; it is absent from the earliest witnesses (Sinaiticus, Vaticanus), and the phrase was later used in debates about Mary's other children.
